newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks surrender gains on political unease.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks surrender gains on political unease.

text.p: Mexican stocks ignored strength in the Dow Friday and surrendered most early gains due to persistent political and social unease, traders said.

"Although the market has been closely linked to developments in the U.S., what's affecting us is the political and social noise that just won't go away," said Alejandro Mercado, an equity analyst at the Banorte brokerage.

Tension was raised when Juan Francisco Ealy Ortiz, editor of major newspaper El Universal surrendered earlier on Friday to police denying charges of tax fraud and accusing the government of censorship.
At 13:30 local time, the leading IPC index was 0.18 percent down at 3,313.02 while the Dow was 1.21 percent up at 5841.85.

Adding to tension in Mexico, police removed a suspicious package from a central square in the capital and reporters said it contained a detonator. Other bomb threats have been reported in recent days, as well as speculation Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrillas may strike during this weekend's Independence Day celebrations.

In other news, Anchor Glass, a U.S. subsidiary of glassmaker Vitro, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Vitro said it had signed a non-binding agreement to sell Anchor's assets to Ball-Foster Glass Container Co.
